output.reason: A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection today for depth, probing and possible infection, which messaging cannot perform.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today for your foot — an urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic or ED can all work. In diabetes, a spreading red, swollen, tender wound on the sole needs hands-on wound inspection and treatment decisions that messaging can't do. Go to an emergency department sooner if you develop fever, chills, spreading redness, blackening skin, or foul drainage. Keep weight off that foot meanwhile.
differential: Deeper diabetic foot infection or early abscess/ulcer

output.vitalSigns: No vital sign readings reported; she states "No fever" but no measured temperature, heart rate, blood pressure or glucose value is given and whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Only consumer summaries and an ED reference synthesis are available; neither establishes remote-management eligibility for this individual diabetic foot wound.
